name: Aspirin mask
lead: An aspirin mask is a home paste made by crushing aspirin tablets, applied to the face, mainly for acne and redness. Proponents note that aspirin is related to salicylic acid, a common acne ingredient.
Aspirin is acetylsalicylic acid and is broken down in the body to salicylic acid [1]. Wikipedia's aspirin article does not discuss acne use, and no studies of aspirin masks were found.

paras: Aspirin is produced by acetylating salicylic acid, and it is readily converted to salicylic acid in the body [1]. Wikipedia mentions topical aspirin only in the context of possible effectiveness for some neuropathic pain [1].

Oral aspirin is associated with stomach upset, ulcers, bleeding and worsening asthma, and is not recommended in late pregnancy or for children with viral infections because of Reye syndrome [1]. These effects relate to oral use; the sources do not describe topical masks.

card.summary: Crushed-aspirin face paste for acne; relies on its link to salicylic acid, with no studies found.
card.note: Oral aspirin has documented warnings; topical mask effects are not described in sources reviewed.

quick.overview:
People crush aspirin tablets into a paste and apply it to the face for acne.

The idea rests on aspirin's relation to salicylic acid; no studies of the mask were found.
quick.mechanism: Aspirin converts to salicylic acid in the body; believers expect a similar anti-acne effect topically, which is untested.
quick.risks: Documented warnings concern oral aspirin; topical risks are not described in the sources reviewed.
